summary: Keep replication application failures on the current route; only transport failures select fallback

replay.detail: No graph replay, admission or envelope changes.

schema.detail: No persisted schema, status fields or diagnostic additions. Route classification is worker-local typed error context.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or coordinated fleet upgrade.

compatibility.detail: Only outbound connect, request/response stream, HTTP transport timeout and carrier-unavailable errors advance routes. Backend, metadata budget, HTTP error status, authentication/grant, protocol, builder, Fabric usage and ambiguous errors remain on the current route with normal backoff. Fabric typed fault errors remain eligible for fallback; untyped legacy errors are conservative application failures. Existing successful-fallback preferred retry remains bounded at 60 seconds. Wire formats and limits are unchanged.

downtime.detail: Normal binary upgrade; no service migration. No live timing or deployment evidence is claimed.

manual.detail: No configuration changes required. Correct backend/protocol/budget/authentication failures rather than expecting another carrier to repair them.

recovery.detail: Application errors retain the current route and connection pool. Grant refusals now use normal peer backoff without route-skipping or the former 24–36 minute route cooldown. Broken transports still discard the HTTP pool and may try the next route. Reverting restores the previous worker policy without reversing state changes.
